# Summary of Cairn Rules

## Rule C1: Single Pulse
When you pulse a cairn, it grows by its stride amount plus an additional amount equal to how many complete strides fit into its current height.
- Formula: New Height = Current Height + Stride + floor(Current Height / Stride)

## Rule C2: Repeated Pulses
Each pulse must be calculated fresh from the new height after the previous pulse. You can't use shortcuts or pre-calculate—the full strides count changes with each pulse because the height changes.

## Rule C3: Leak
A leak removes marks after a pulse based on the new pulsed height. For each complete group of the leak size that fits into the pulsed height, one mark is lost.
- Order matters: pulse first, then apply leak to the result

## Rule C4: Finding the Origin
You can work backwards from a final height to find the starting height by reversing pulses one at a time. Each final height comes from exactly one origin, so there's no ambiguity.

## Rule C5: Drain
A drain removes a fixed number of marks after each pulse cycle. You must cycle through one at a time because each pulse adds a different amount (the full strides count keeps changing). The cairn eventually empties when the drain removes more than each pulse adds.

## Rule C6: Merging
Two cairns combine into one using weighted contributions from each. The share determines what percentage of each cairn contributes (as decimal proportions), floors are applied to each contribution, and then a tether value is added.
- Formula: floor(w × q₁) + floor((1-w) × q₂) + b
